methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops by a Norfolk native signal grassroots peer-to-peer capability building outside traditional tech hubs, directly addressing the technology gap through distributed, accessible skill development.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in deep AI workforce preparation beyond NoVA, potentially creating regional nodes of expertise that could catalyze distributed capability if paired with peer learning networks.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Commentary explicitly naming the urban-rural divide created by AI data center concentration signals awareness that infrastructure investment alone doesn't distribute capability—economic benefits accrue to metro areas while rural regions bear costs without gaining expertise.

signals.title: Richmond summer program helps visually impaired students explore careers in technology and cybersecurity - WTVR.com
signals.signal_reading: Specialized technology and cybersecurity career program for visually impaired students demonstrates Richmond's capacity for niche, deep capability development, but serving a specific population suggests concentrated rather than broadly distributed access.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Virginia Tech adds an artificial intelligence minor to its curriculum - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's new AI minor creates formal pathways for deep technical skill development in the New River Valley, positioning the region to generate homegrown expertise that could distribute through alumni networks statewide.
